**Finding: IP — compliant (meets fallback, largely preferred). No redline proposed.**

Section 4 works in our favour:

- **Ownership of deliverables (p0017):** all work product required by a Statement of Work — the "Works" — "are the property of Company" once invoiced and paid, i.e. ownership vests in Clear Capital rather than a licence-back structure.
- **Assignment language (p0033):** on termination Contractor "hereby assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress."
- **Vendor pre-existing IP / generic tools (p0020):** Contractor retains only its own software, methodologies, tools, know-how and techniques not created for us — the permitted vendor-retention carve-out.
- **Embedded Vendor IP licence (p0021):** royalty-free, perpetual, sublicensable licence to use, copy, modify and create derivatives for our business operations; supported by p0022 (we may modify the software and engage others after payment or termination without further payment).
- **Customer Data (p0040):** no standing Contractor licence in our data; Confidential Information (our records, data, reports) may not be used or disclosed without our express prior written permission. No joint ownership and no assignment of our IP or data to Contractor anywhere in the document.

Noted in the rationale but not redlined (sub-preferred wording only): the embedded-IP licence is not expressly "irrevocable" or "worldwide" (though perpetual and subject to no revocation or territorial mechanic), there is no affirmative "we retain all rights in our data" sentence, and §4(b)(ii) limits resale/use of Contractor's administrative records. If the drafting window is open, we would ask for "irrevocable and worldwide" and a one-line Customer Data ownership statement, but neither gap justifies a deviation.
